title: USA defeats China 94-61 in FIBA Women's World Cup opener; Clark records 14 points and 11 assists
dek: Caitlin Clark finished with 14 points and 11 assists in her World Cup debut as the United States defeated China 94-61 on Friday, September 4 in Berlin. The victory extended the US win streak to 31 consecutive games. Nine of the 12 players on the American roster were making their first World Cup appearance.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Clark's 11 assists marked the most by an American in a Women's World Cup debut, according to Sporting News reporting.
bottom_line: Clark's elite playmaking in her first World Cup game sets a high bar for the American offensive rhythm; whether the US can maintain this efficiency and ball movement through the group stage against Italy and the Czech Republic will show whether the new roster's chemistry is sustainable beyond a blowout opener.
body: The United States opened its FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup campaign with a decisive 94-61 victory over China on Friday, September 4, in a group-stage game in Berlin. Caitlin Clark recorded 14 points and 11 assists in her World Cup debut, anchoring an American offense that benefited from deep offensive firepower and elite ball movement.

Clark's 11 assists marked the most by an American in a Women's World Cup debut, per Sporting News reporting. The Guardian reports that Clark's 11 assists were the most by a US player since Dawn Staley had 12 against Russia in 1998, though the same outlet also reports a separate claim that Clark's 11 assists tied her for the most ever with Teresa Edwards, who had a dozen against China in 1986. These two figures appear to reference different historical records and remain unresolved in available reporting.

Paige Bueckers and Rhyne Howard each added 14 points, joining Clark atop the American scoring column. According to Sporting News, all 12 players on Team USA's roster scored, and Angel Reese contributed five points and a team-high nine rebounds in 17 minutes off the bench. Bueckers said in the Guardian's reporting, "It's just organic. We know how to play well off of each other. She draws so much defensive attention, so a lot of the defense is worried about her."

Clark played 25 minutes and finished with three rebounds. According to Sporting News, she became the first player in tournament history to finish with at least 10 assists and no turnovers. Clark was named Team USA's Player of the Game.

China's 7-foot-3-inch Zhang Ziyu finished with 13 points, making nine of her 10 free throws and blocking two shots. The Guardian reports Zhang was 19 years old. Clark acknowledged the defensive challenge: "This was a different type of basketball game that I probably ever played in my entire life. I've never played against a woman of that size. She obviously presented some challenges for us, but you gotta give our post players a lot of credit."

US frontcourt players Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Aliyah Boston and Angel Reese collected a combined 24 rebounds, per the Guardian. The victory extended Team USA's win streak to 31 consecutive games. Nine of the 12 players on the American roster were playing in their first World Cup, per the Guardian.
Team USA has a day off Saturday before facing Italy on Sunday at 2:45 p.m. ET and the Czech Republic on Monday, according to Sporting News reporting.
